// diagnostic E0181

Jet.ConstructorReturnsOtherType

`{type}.new` returns `{result}`, not a `{type}`

What

`{type}.new` returns `{result}`, not a `{type}`

Why

A type's static `new` is its constructor, and a call `{type}.new(…)` reads as making a `{type}`, so any other result misleads every caller

Fix

Make `new` return `{type}`, `{type}?` or `{type}` with a failure contract, or rename the function to say what it returns

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning Jet.ConstructorReturnsOtherType: Tests/UI/constructor_wrong_owner.stderr.

Error: Jet.ConstructorReturnsOtherType: `Celsius.new` returns `Float`, not a `Celsius`
  --> Tests/UI/constructor_wrong_owner.jet:6:32
    |
  6 |     new: fn(degrees: Float) -> Float { degrees }
    |                                ^^^^^
 Why: A type's static `new` is its constructor, and a call `Celsius.new(…)` reads as making a `Celsius`, so any other result misleads every caller
 Fix: Make `new` return `Celsius`, `Celsius?` or `Celsius` with a failure contract, or rename the function to say what it returns
